name: pulse-ability
demonstrates: CYBERPUN-17-10-t3's scene wiring as it is reachable from a running build: the pulse button is visible and tappable from the very first gameplay frame, and pressing it drives PulseAbility.trigger(...) -> pushes/damages any in-radius raccoon -> spawns/replays PulseRingNode's sprite_pulse shockwave, all in GameScene.applyPulseTrigger(raccoons:). WHICH BUTTON THIS TAPS, AND WHY IT MOVED: since PR #63's review decision (CYBERPUN-17-12 PR 2) the run's one visible ability control is the HUD's bottom-RIGHT HUDPulseButton -- the placement the ticket asks for -- and CYBERPUN-17-10's older bottom-left PulseButton mount is GONE: CYBERPUN-17-14 PR 1 deleted Sources/UI/PulseButton.swift, its layoutPulseButton() mount and GameScene.pulseButton outright, so at head there is no second ability control constructed, wired or hidden anywhere in the run (this sentence previously said the old button was 'still constructed and wired', which was true when this journey was written and stale by the time of PR #67 review). The navigate step below therefore targets the bottom-right button; both buttons always drove the same GameScene.handlePulsePress(), so what this journey proves is unchanged. WHAT THIS JOURNEY CAN AND CANNOT SHOW: the ring's full play-through is 8 frames * PulseRingNode.frameDuration (0.03s) = 0.24s -- far shorter than the round-trip latency of a screenshot step (which screenshots the CURRENT frame only after the navigate/tap step's own vision-driven confirmation has already completed), the same timing gap auto-fire-weapons.json documents for bullets/muzzle flashes. A screenshot taken after tapping the button is therefore expected to usually land AFTER the ring has already finished and re-hidden itself, showing the ordinary gameplay screen rather than a mid-shockwave frame -- that is this probe vocabulary's limitation, not evidence the ring failed to play. What this journey DOES reliably prove on a device: the button renders in the correct HUD slot from the first gameplay frame (product gate 8's visibility half) and a press is accepted without the app crashing or hanging (no raccoon needs to be in range for PulseAbility.trigger(...) to fire and return a Result -- see that method's own 'Result.hits is empty, not nil, when nothing was in range' contract). The push/damage/ring-spawn pipeline itself, and the same-update-tick timing the acceptance criteria call for, are pinned end-to-end (not merely screenshot-reviewed) by PulseSceneWiringTests, which drives GameScene.applyPulseTrigger(raccoons:) directly against a hand-built raccoon and asserts on its resulting position/hp and on PulseRingNode's action/visibility state -- exactly the class of behaviour a probe screenshot cannot reliably catch given the animation's own short duration. Gate is human/vision review of the two screenshots below (mainly: is the pulse button visibly present and does the app stay foregrounded after the tap); assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive. ALSO REVIEWED FOR CYBERPUN-17-14 GATE 8 (this journey carries that story's tag too): what these frames CAN show is gate 8's visibility/no-crash half -- the button present in the correct HUD slot and the app staying foregrounded after a press. What these frames typically CANNOT show, for the reasons already stated above (screenshot timing vs. the ring's 0.24s play window, and no raccoon is guaranteed in range on this journey): the ring drawn mid-shockwave, raccoons visibly mid-shove, or a raccoon pinned against a building. Those three visual claims are audited and code-verified instead (see docs/evidence/gate-08-pulse-audit.txt) and remain outstanding for literal capture, which needs a different vantage (raccoons in range near a building at the moment of a press) than this journey provides.

steps.target: the large neon-outlined PLAY button in the middle of the title screen that starts a new run (NOT the plain HIGH SCORES button below it)
steps.expect: the running game -- a playable isometric city scene with a ground lattice, buildings and a player actor, not a menu or title screen

steps.target: the round pulse-ability button in the bottom-RIGHT corner of the screen (the HUD's own button, on the opposite side from the round movement thumbstick)
steps.expect: the same running gameplay screen, still showing the isometric city and player, with the app still foregrounded after the tap
